title: Toggleable Textures
description: Toggleable Textures is a client-side Fabric mod that lets players switch selected Minecraft block textures between modern and nostalgic historical versions through an in-game menu.
body:
Special thanks to [CodecraftPlugin](https://github.com/codecraftplugin) for the art for the image!

Toggleable Textures is a client-side Fabric mod that lets you switch selected Minecraft block textures between modern and nostalgic historical versions through an in-game menu.

Search for supported blocks, preview texture choices, cycle between available versions, and click Apply to update textures without replacing the entire game with a full resource pack.

Older textures are extracted from your local Minecraft installation, so the mod does not ship Mojang assets.

## Features

- Per-block texture selection
- Minecraft-style in-game menu
- Search bar for supported blocks
- Preview icons for selected textures
- Apply button so textures only reload when you choose
- Client-side only

## Installation

### Modrinth App

Install Toggleable Textures like any other Fabric mod through the Modrinth App.

Make sure Fabric API is installed. If it is listed as a dependency, the Modrinth App should handle that automatically.

### Manual Install

1. Install Fabric Loader for the supported Minecraft version. (26.2
https://fabricmc.net/use/installer/)
2. Install Fabric API. (https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api)
3. Download ToggleableTextures. (Download the .jar file here.)
4. Place the `.jar` file in your `.minecraft/mods` folder.
5. Launch Minecraft with the Fabric profile. (Before doing so, read IMPORTANT below!)

## Important: Old Texture Support

To use the older texture options, launch Minecraft 1.5.1, 1.12.2, and 1.13.2 once from the vanilla Minecraft Launcher.

This gives Toggleable Textures access to your own local files so it can extract the old textures on your computer.

## How To Use

1. Open Minecraft with the mod installed.
2. Join a world.
3. Press `=` to open the Toggleable Textures menu.
4. Search for a block or scroll through the list.
5. Click the texture button to switch between available versions.
6. Click Apply to reload the selected textures.
